subject: english
topic: Oral English: consonant sounds and clusters

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word whose underlined consonant sound is different from the others. All the words begin with the letters 'CH'.
A. CHAIR
B. CHEMIST
C. CHURCH
D. CHEESE
kept.explanation: CHAIR, CHURCH and CHEESE all begin with the sound /tʃ/ as in 'chop'. CHEMIST begins with the sound /k/ instead. So CHEMIST is the odd one out.
kept.pidgin: CHAIR, CHURCH and CHEESE all dey start with /tʃ/ sound like 'chop'. But CHEMIST dey start with /k/ sound. So na CHEMIST be the odd one.

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that begins with a consonant cluster.
A. SPLASH
B. TABLE
C. WATER
D. APPLE
kept.explanation: SPLASH begins with three consonant sounds together, /spl/, which is a consonant cluster. TABLE, WATER and APPLE do not start with clustered consonant sounds.
kept.pidgin: SPLASH dey start with /spl/ wey be three consonant sounds join together, na so consonant cluster dey be. TABLE, WATER and APPLE no get that kind start.

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that has a silent consonant.
A. CASTLE
B. CAMEL
C. CARROT
D. CABBAGE
kept.explanation: In CASTLE, the letter 't' is silent, so it is pronounced /ˈkɑːsəl/. The other words have all their consonants pronounced.
kept.pidgin: For CASTLE, the 't' no dey pronounce, dem dey call am /ˈkɑːsəl/. The other words dey pronounce all their consonants well well.

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that contains the consonant sound /θ/ as heard in 'think'.
A. THESE
B. MOTHER
C. THIRD
D. FATHER
kept.explanation: THIRD is pronounced with the voiceless sound /θ/, just like 'think'. THESE, MOTHER and FATHER all contain the voiced sound /ð/ instead.
kept.pidgin: THIRD dey use the voiceless /θ/ sound, the same way as 'think'. THESE, MOTHER and FATHER dey use /ð/ sound wey be voiced one.

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that ends with a consonant cluster.
A. TEXT
B. TRAY
C. TABLE
D. TOMATO
kept.explanation: TEXT ends with the sounds /kst/, which is a cluster of three consonant sounds together. TRAY, TABLE and TOMATO do not end with clustered consonant sounds.
kept.pidgin: TEXT dey end with /kst/, wey be three consonant sounds join finish. TRAY, TABLE and TOMATO no get that kind ending.

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that ends with the same consonant sound as the word in capitals.
BRIDGE
A. REACH
B. JUDGE
C. WATCH
D. BENCH
kept.explanation: BRIDGE ends with the voiced sound /dʒ/. JUDGE also ends with /dʒ/. REACH, WATCH and BENCH all end with the voiceless sound /tʃ/ instead.
kept.pidgin: BRIDGE dey end with /dʒ/ sound wey be voiced. JUDGE too dey end with /dʒ/. REACH, WATCH and BENCH dey end with /tʃ/ wey no be voiced.

kept.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that does NOT begin with a three-consonant cluster.
A. STRAY
B. SPRAY
C. STOP
D. SCREAM
kept.explanation: STRAY begins with /str/, SPRAY with /spr/, and SCREAM with /skr/, each having three consonant sounds together. STOP only begins with /st/, which is a two-consonant cluster, so it does not fit the three-consonant pattern.
kept.pidgin: STRAY dey start with /str/, SPRAY with /spr/, SCREAM with /skr/, all na three consonant sounds join together. STOP na only /st/, na two consonant sounds, e no match the three-consonant pattern.
